def-cls-cluster.title: Clustered errors with compound symmetry
def-cls-cluster.html:
The n observations fall into G clusters, cluster g containing mg of them, with n=∑gmg. The model is 𝛃𝛆Y=Xβ+ε with 𝛆Eε=0 and 𝛆Cov(ε)=V=diag(Σ1,…,ΣG),Σg=σ2{(1−ρ)Img+ρ11⊤},{#eq-cls-compound}

a block diagonal matrix with one block per cluster. This covariance is called compound symmetry or equicorrelation, and ρ is the intraclass correlation. The matrix is positive definite iff −1/(maxgmg−1)<ρ<1. The clusters are balanced if mg=m for all g.

def-cls-covariance.title: Covariance models for a subject’s observations
def-cls-covariance.title_html: Covariance models for a subject’s observations
def-cls-covariance.html:
Let subject i be observed at times ti1<⋯<timi, and write Σi for the covariance matrix of its response vector, with entries σjk and time gap djk=|tij−tik|. The standard models are

Model σjk Parameters
independence σ2δjk 1
compound symmetry σu2+σ2δjk 2
first-order autoregressive σ2ρ|j−k| 2
exponential (spatial power) σ2ρdjk 2
autoregressive plus random intercept σu2+σ2ρ|j−k| 3
Toeplitz of order q σ2c|j−k|, with c0=1 and cu=0 for u≥q q
random intercept and slope (1,tij)D(1,tik)⊤+σ2δjk 4
unstructured σjk, unrestricted m(m+1)/2

Each model must also be nonnegative definite; the constraint is σu2,σ2≥0 and |ρ|<1 for the first five, D nonnegative definite for the random-coefficient model, and a genuine restriction on (c1,…,cq−1) for the Toeplitz model (@exr-cls-toeplitz-pd).

def-cls-sphericity.title: Sphericity and Box’s measure
def-cls-sphericity.html:
Let Σ be an m×m positive definite matrix and U as above. Σ satisfies sphericity if U⊤ΣU=λIm−1 for some λ>0. Box’s measure of sphericity is ϵ(Σ)={trΨ}2(m−1)tr(Ψ2),Ψ=U⊤ΣU.{#eq-cls-epsilon}

Neither the condition nor ϵ depends on the choice of U: two such matrices satisfy U~=UQ with Q orthogonal, so Ψ~=Q⊤ΨQ has the same trace, the same trace of square, and is a multiple of the identity exactly when Ψ is.

def-cls-splitplot.title: The balanced split-plot model
def-cls-splitplot.html:
Index blocks by i=1,…,r, whole-plot treatments by j=1,…,a and subplot treatments by k=1,…,b, and write yijk for the response on the subplot of block i receiving whole-plot treatment j and subplot treatment k. The split-plot model is yijk=μ+ξi+ωj+ηij+τk+γjk+eijk,{#eq-cls-splitplot-model}

where ξi, ωj, τk and γjk are fixed effects, the ηij are uncorrelated whole-plot errors with mean zero and variance σw2, the eijk are uncorrelated subplot errors with mean zero and variance σs2, and the two sets are uncorrelated with each other. The normal split-plot model takes both sets to be normal.

exm-cls-clusters.title: Forty clusters of five
exm-cls-clusters.html: Take G=40 clusters of m=5, with ρ=0.4, σ2=1, one cluster-level and one within-cluster regressor besides the intercept, so pb=2 and pw=1. Then λw=2.6 and λs=0.6, and the design effects are exactly 2.60 and 0.60, as the listing confirms from the full 200×200 covariance matrix. By @eq-cls-naive-s2, E(s2)={2.6(38)+0.6(159)}/197=0.9858, so the reported variance of the cluster-level coefficient is 0.379 times the truth and that of the within-cluster coefficient 1.643 times the truth. A nominal 95% interval for the first is about 1.62 times too short, and the simulation below finds its coverage to be 0.759.

exm-cls-grip.title: Grip strength over six visits
exm-cls-grip.html:
Twenty-four patients have grip strength measured, in kilograms, at six weekly visits, simulated from 𝛍N6(μ,Σ) with Σ first-order autoregressive, σjk=4×0.6|j−k|, and a mean drifting slowly upward; the observed occasion means are 47.818, 48.099, 49.056, 49.177, 49.561 and 49.263 kg. The true Box measure is ϵ=0.700: adjacent visits correlate 0.6 and visits five weeks apart only 0.65, so adjacent differences are much less variable than distant ones. The four analyses of H give

Analysis statistic degrees of freedom p
univariate, uncorrected 4.770 5, 115 0.0005
Greenhouse–Geisser, ϵ^=0.645 4.770 3.23, 74.2 0.0035
Huynh–Feldt, ϵ~=0.763 4.770 3.81, 87.7 0.0019
multivariate 3.605 5, 19 0.0184

All four reject, but the evidence differs by a factor of nearly forty between first and last. Distrust the uncorrected test: its nominal degrees of freedom are too large by the factor ϵ.

exm-cls-grunfeld-covariance.title: Investment in eleven firms
exm-cls-grunfeld-covariance.html:
Grunfeld’s panel records gross investment, market value and capital stock for 11 US firms in each of the 20 years from 1935 to 1954, a complete rectangle with n=220. Take log investment as the response and the mean model E(y)=β0+β1t+β2log⁡(value), with t in decades from the middle of the record, so p=3. An unstructured covariance would need 210 parameters from 11 subjects, which is hopeless. Fitting the alternatives by restricted maximum likelihood gives

Covariance model q −2ℓR AICR BICR
independence 1 476.95 478.95 482.33
compound symmetry 2 114.83 118.83 125.59
autoregressive 2 49.89 53.89 60.65
autoregressive + random intercept 3 29.87 35.87 46.01
random intercept and slope 4 98.66 106.66 120.18
Toeplitz of order 4 4 147.97 155.97 169.49

Independence is hopeless: the firms differ enormously in size, and log investment is nearly constant within a firm relative to the spread between firms. Compound symmetry captures that and improves −2ℓR by 362, the autoregressive model on the same two parameters does better still, and the combination is best on both criteria, by 82.96 of AICR over compound symmetry. The random-coefficient model, which gives each firm its own trend, describes these data worse than a persistent level plus decaying serial correlation.

Figure 33.4.1 shows why. The residual correlations are 0.953 at one year, 0.918 at two, 0.884 at five and 0.839 at ten: high everywhere, because the firm’s level dominates, but visibly decaying, which compound symmetry cannot reproduce. The variogram rises to a plateau of about 0.099, far below the total residual variance of 0.4839; the gap is the between-firm variance. The selected model is not innocent either: its fitted correlogram flattens onto its own floor after three or four years while the data go on decaying. That is what the diagnostic is for, and a reason to read the empirical standard error of @prp-cls-selection(b) alongside the model-based one.

With the selected model the coefficient of log⁡(value) is 0.6295, with a model-based standard error of 0.0712 and an empirical one of 0.0608, and the coefficient of t is 0.4261 with standard errors 0.0600 and 0.0601. Ordinary least squares, treating the 220 observations as independent, reports 0.9833 and 0.3768 with standard errors 0.0351 and 0.0821. The two disagree substantially about the elasticity with respect to market value, because least squares reads it mostly from differences between firms while generalized least squares, having absorbed the firm levels into the covariance, reads it from movements within firms — the between-versus-within distinction of Section 6.6 again, and a question about the subject matter.

exm-cls-grunfeld-growth.title: The investment trajectories of eleven firms
exm-cls-grunfeld-growth.title_html: The investment trajectories of eleven firms
exm-cls-grunfeld-growth.html:
The panel of @exm-cls-grunfeld-covariance, seen a third time — after the random firm effect of Chapter 32 and the covariance models of Section 33.4 — now with a straight line in t (decades from the middle of the record) whose intercept and slope vary by firm. The within-firm residual standard deviation is σ^=0.2797, and D^=(2.36350.04550.04550.0361), so firms’ log-investment levels have standard deviation 1.5374 — enormous, the difference between General Motors and Diamond Match — and their slopes 0.1899 per decade, correlated 0.156 with the level. Maximizing the restricted likelihood numerically returns the same three values to four decimals, as @prp-cls-growth(c) predicts.

The population curve has intercept 3.9109 and slope 0.5577 per decade, with standard errors 0.4639 and 0.0659 from @eq-cls-growth-beta; the slope is 8.46 standard errors from zero. The shrinkage matrix is W=(0.99830.00160.00480.7496), so intercepts are left alone — with twenty observations per firm a firm’s own level is known almost exactly — while slopes are pulled a quarter of the way towards the population slope. The firms’ own slopes span 0.158 to 0.943, the predicted slopes 0.248 to 0.846, a standard deviation 0.755 times that of the raw slopes; the largest adjustment is IBM’s, from 0.943 to 0.846. Figure 33.5.1 shows the eleven firms with all three lines.

For the last year of the record, t=0.95, the predicted value on a firm’s own curve has standard error 0.1102, against 1.6461 for a firm outside the data — fifteen times larger, and simulation from the fitted model confirms both, at 0.1103 and 1.6603. The interval for a new firm, 1.214 to 7.667 on the log scale, is nearly useless, and rightly so: without knowing a firm’s size, its investment cannot be predicted within three orders of magnitude.

exm-cls-irrigation.title: An irrigation and variety trial
exm-cls-irrigation.html:
Four fields are each divided into three whole plots, and the regimes flood, sprinkler and drip are assigned at random within each field; each whole plot is divided into four subplots carrying four barley varieties in random order, giving n=48 yields in tonnes per hectare, simulated from @eq-cls-splitplot-model with σw=0.35 and σs=0.25 t/ha. The analysis of variance is

Source df SS MS F p
blocks 3 9.471 3.157
irrigation A 2 9.215 4.608 10.637 0.0106
whole-plot error 6 2.599 0.433
variety C 3 1.755 0.585 9.442 0.0002
irrigation × variety 6 0.958 0.160 2.577 0.0419
subplot error 27 1.673 0.062

The two error mean squares differ by a factor of seven. Solving @eq-cls-splitplot-ems gives σ^s=MSE=0.2489 and σ^w=(MSAB−MSE)/b=0.3046, close to the generating values.

The irrigation means are 4.8075, 5.8000 and 5.6575 t/ha; a difference of two has standard error 2MSAB/(rb)=0.2327 on 6 degrees of freedom, so drip beats flood by 0.8500 t/ha with t=3.653. The variety means are 5.134, 5.364, 5.574 and 5.614, and a difference of two has standard error 2MSE/(ra)=0.1016 on 27 degrees of freedom — more than twice as precise, from the same 48 observations. Comparing drip with flood for one variety is neither: by @eq-cls-splitplot-simple its standard error is {MSAB+3MSE}/8=0.2782, on 11.77 Satterthwaite degrees of freedom.

exr-cls-blup-not-unbiased.title: A2
exr-cls-blup-not-unbiased.html: The predicted curves are less spread out than the true ones. Is this a bias? Compute E(u^i) and Cov(u^i) and compare the latter with D.

exr-cls-crve-bias.title: C2
exr-cls-crve-bias.html: Show that 𝛆𝛆E(Xg⊤ε^gε^g⊤Xg)≠Xg⊤ΣgXg in general, by writing 𝛆𝛆𝛆ε^g=εg−Xg(X⊤X)−1X⊤ε and expanding, and show that the leading correction is of order p/G. Why is the bias downward, and what does this suggest about the factor G/(G−1)⋅(n−1)/(n−p) used in the coverage simulation behind Figure 33.2.1?

exr-cls-crve-steps.title: C1
exr-cls-crve-steps.html: Carry out in detail the three steps of the cluster-sandwich argument above, with the constants: show that (K1)–(K3) give ‖Xg‖≤mmaxC and 𝛆E‖Xg⊤εg‖2≤mmax2C2K1/2; that 𝛆𝛆Var(a⊤Xg⊤(εgεg⊤−Σg)Xga) is bounded uniformly in g; and that 𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃n−1∑g‖tg‖2≤mmax2C2(β^−β)⊤An(β^−β). Where exactly does the number of clusters, rather than of observations, enter?

exr-cls-cs-implies-sphericity.title: B1
exr-cls-cs-implies-sphericity.html: Show directly that compound symmetry Σ=σ2{(1−ρ)I+ρ11⊤} gives Ψ=σ2(1−ρ)Im−1, and hence that the split-plot analysis of @thm-cls-splitplot is the repeated-measures F test with ϵ=1. Which λ of @lem-cls-hf-form does it correspond to?

exr-cls-effective-n.title: A2
exr-cls-effective-n.html: A trial can afford n=1200 pupils and must randomize schools, not pupils, to the two arms. The intraclass correlation of the outcome is ρ=0.10. Compare the effective sample size for 12 schools of 100 pupils, 40 schools of 30, and 120 schools of 10.

exr-cls-epsilon-ar1.title: A2
exr-cls-epsilon-ar1.html: For m=3 and an autoregressive covariance σjk=ρ|j−k| with 0<ρ<1, compute Ψ for the basis u1=(1,−1,0)⊤/2, u2=(1,1,−2)⊤/6 and show that sphericity fails. Which pairwise difference has the largest variance?

exr-cls-growth-negative-d.title: C1
exr-cls-growth-negative-d.html: Simulate data for which D^ of @eq-cls-growth-reml is not nonnegative definite. Describe what the restricted maximum likelihood estimate does instead, relate it to the boundary problem of @prp-mix-inference, and explain why the two-stage estimate is nevertheless unbiased for D.

exr-cls-growth-quadratic.title: B1
exr-cls-growth-quadratic.html: Suppose the fixed effects use a quadratic in time, X=[1,t,t2], but the random effects only a line, Z=[1,t]. Show that C(ΣX)⊆C(X) still holds, and identify what changes in 𝛃Cov(β^). What if instead the random effects used the quadratic and the fixed effects only the line?

exr-cls-growth-unbalanced.title: B2
exr-cls-growth-unbalanced.html: Let subject i be observed at its own times, giving Xi of full column rank p, and let bi=(Xi⊤Xi)−1Xi⊤yi. Show that 𝛃bi∼(β,D+σ2(Xi⊤Xi)−1) independently over i, and deduce that the generalized least squares estimate from the bi is 𝛃β^=(∑iWi)−1∑iWibi with Wi={D+σ2(Xi⊤Xi)−1}−1, a precision-weighted average of the subjects’ own curves. Recover @eq-cls-growth-beta as the balanced case.

exr-cls-icc-range.title: A1
exr-cls-icc-range.html: Show from @prp-cls-compound(a) that the compound symmetric matrix is positive definite iff −1/(m−1)<ρ<1, and that the random-effects representation εi=ug(i)+ei forces ρ≥0. Give a mechanism that produces ρ<0.

exr-cls-model-count.title: A1
exr-cls-model-count.html: A trial measures 60 patients at 8 visits. How many parameters does each model of @def-cls-covariance need? Which could not be fitted with only 10 patients, and why?

exr-cls-more-subplots.title: A2
exr-cls-more-subplots.html: With r, a, σw2 and σs2 fixed, what happens to the variance of a whole-plot contrast, and to that of a subplot contrast, as b grows? Which kind of comparison does adding subplots help?

exr-cls-power-comparison.title: C1
exr-cls-power-comparison.html: For m=4, N=20 and Σ compound symmetric, compare by simulation the power of the uncorrected univariate test, the Greenhouse–Geisser test and the multivariate test of @prp-cls-multivariate against a linear trend in the occasion means. Repeat with an autoregressive Σ of the same total variance. Which would you choose if you knew the alternative were a linear trend, and why is a single contrast better still?

exr-cls-reml-boundary.title: C1
exr-cls-reml-boundary.html: The autoregressive model is nested in the autoregressive-plus-random-intercept model at σu2=0, a boundary of the parameter space. Explain why the likelihood ratio statistic comparing the two does not have a χ2(1) null distribution, state what it does have (@prp-mix-inference), and say what this means for reading AICR differences as informal evidence.

exr-cls-reml-comparison.title: B1
exr-cls-reml-comparison.html: Two analysts fit the investment data of @exm-cls-grunfeld-covariance. The first uses the mean model of the example with an autoregressive covariance; the second adds a quadratic term in t and uses compound symmetry. They compare AICR. Explain what is wrong, and describe a correct sequence of comparisons.

exr-cls-rm-mixed-equivalence.title: B2
exr-cls-rm-mixed-equivalence.html: Consider the mixed model yij=μj+ui+eij with ui and eij independent normal, of variances σu2 and σe2. Show that restricted maximum likelihood gives σ^e2=MSE and σ^u2=(MSS−MSE)/m when this is nonnegative, where MSS is the between-subject mean square, and that the Wald statistic for H:μ1=⋯=μm, divided by m−1, is the uncorrected F of @eq-cls-rm-ss.

exr-cls-shrinkage-scalar.title: A1
exr-cls-shrinkage-scalar.html: Take p=1, so X=1m and each subject has a single random level. Show that W reduces to σu2/(σu2+σ2/m) and that the predictor is the shrunken mean 𝛃𝛃β^+W(y¯i−β^). What happens as m→∞, and as σu2→0?

exr-cls-sphericity-two.title: A1
exr-cls-sphericity-two.html: Show that every 2×2 covariance matrix satisfies sphericity, so that with m=2 the repeated-measures F test is exact whatever Σ is. Identify the test in that case.

exr-cls-split-split.title: C1
exr-cls-split-split.html: A split-split-plot design divides each subplot into c sub-subplots and randomizes a third factor D among them, adding an error ζijk of variance σu2 shared by the sub-subplots of a subplot. Write down the covariance matrix in the style of @eq-cls-splitplot-cov, find its three eigenvalues and eigenspaces, and state which effects are tested against which of the three error mean squares.

exr-cls-splitplot-kruskal.title: B1
exr-cls-splitplot-kruskal.html: Verify @thm-cls-splitplot(a) directly from @thm-proj-kruskal by computing VX for the model matrix X=[1,B,A,C,AC] of indicator columns. Then show that adding the block-by-A columns leaves the condition true but destroys the analysis, and say why.

exr-cls-splitplot-reml.title: B2
exr-cls-splitplot-reml.html: Show that for the balanced split-plot model the restricted likelihood of (σw2,σs2) depends on the data only through SSAB and SSE, and that it is maximized at λ^w=MSAB, λ^s=MSE provided MSAB≥MSE. Hint: the error contrasts span C(PAB)⊕C(PE), and V acts as a scalar on each.

exr-cls-strata-membership.title: A1
exr-cls-strata-membership.html: For the design of @exm-cls-irrigation, say which stratum each of the following belongs to, and on how many degrees of freedom its error is estimated: the difference between two block means; between two variety means; between two irrigation means; between two varieties within the drip regime; the difference in the effect of drip versus flood between two varieties; and the difference between drip and flood for the first variety alone.

exr-cls-toeplitz-pd.title: B2
exr-cls-toeplitz-pd.html: Show that the Toeplitz model of @def-cls-covariance with q=3 is nonnegative definite for every m iff (1,c1,c2,0,…) is the autocorrelation sequence of a moving-average process of order two, and explain why the parameterization cu∝∑lalal+u used in the listing above satisfies this automatically.

exr-cls-two-strata-decomposition.title: B1
exr-cls-two-strata-decomposition.html: Let X=[Xb,Xw] as in @prp-cls-compound(b), with 1∈C(Xb). Show that M=Mb+Mw with Mb and Mw the projections onto C(Xb) and C(Xw), that the residual sum of squares splits into a between-cluster and a within-cluster part, and that the two corresponding mean squares are unbiased for λw and λs.

exr-cls-unequal-clusters.title: B2
exr-cls-unequal-clusters.html: Let the clusters have unequal sizes mg. Show that V of @eq-cls-compound has eigenvalues σ2{1+(mg−1)ρ}, one per cluster, together with σ2(1−ρ) with multiplicity n−G. Deduce that 1 is an eigenvector only if all clusters have the same size, so that the intercept alone breaks @prp-cls-compound(b).

exr-cls-variogram-shapes.title: A2
exr-cls-variogram-shapes.html: Sketch the population variogram γ(u) for compound symmetry, for the autoregressive model and for their combination, marking the total variance on each. Which feature identifies σu2, and which identifies measurement error?

lem-cls-hf-form.title: Equivalent forms of sphericity
lem-cls-hf-form.html:
For a positive definite m×m matrix Σ the following are equivalent:

  1. U⊤ΣU=λIm−1;

  2. Var(Yj−Yk)=2λ for every j≠k;

  3. σjk=aj+ak+λδjk for some a1,…,am, where δjk is one if j=k and zero otherwise;

  4. Σ=λI+1a⊤+a1⊤ for some a∈Rm.

Moreover 1/(m−1)≤ϵ(Σ)≤1, with ϵ=1 iff sphericity holds, and compound symmetry implies sphericity but not conversely.

lem-cls-strata.title: The two error strata
lem-cls-strata.html:
Let V be as in @eq-cls-splitplot-cov and put λw=σs2+bσw2 and λs=σs2. Then:

  1. PW=Ir⊗Ia⊗J¯b, and V=λwPW+λs(I−PW), so V has the two eigenvalues λw and λs with eigenspaces C(PW) and C(PW)⊥, of dimensions ra and ra(b−1).

  2. The six matrices of @eq-cls-splitplot-projections together with PE are mutually orthogonal projections summing to I, with ranks 1, r−1, a−1, (r−1)(a−1), b−1, (a−1)(b−1) and (r−1)a(b−1).

  3. P0,PB,PA,PAB have their ranges inside C(PW), and PC,PAC,PE have their ranges inside C(PW)⊥. Hence VP=λwP for the first four and VP=λsP for the last three.

prp-cls-box.title: The moment-matched approximation
prp-cls-box.html:
Under the assumptions of @thm-cls-sphericity, with H true, write ϵ=ϵ(Σ), d1=m−1 and d2=(N−1)(m−1). Then

  1. ESST=trΨ, VarSST=2tr(Ψ2), ESSE=(N−1)trΨ and VarSSE=2(N−1)tr(Ψ2).

  2. The scaled chi-squared variable gχ2(h) matching the first two moments of SST has h=ϵd1 and g=tr(Ψ2)/trΨ; the one matching SSE has h′=ϵd2 and the same g. Since SST and SSE are independent by @thm-cls-sphericity(a), replacing each by its matched scaled chi-squared gives the approximation F≈F(ϵd1,ϵd2), which is exact when ϵ=1.

prp-cls-compound.title: Compound symmetry and the design effect
prp-cls-compound.title_html: Compound symmetry and the design effect
prp-cls-compound.html:
Let @eq-cls-compound hold with mg=m for all g, let λw=σ2{1+(m−1)ρ} and λs=σ2(1−ρ), and let rank(X)=p.

  1. V=λwPW+λs(I−PW). Its eigenvalues are λw with multiplicity G and λs with multiplicity n−G, and V−1=1λs(I−mρ1+(m−1)ρPW).

  2. C(VX)⊆C(X) iff C(PWX)⊆C(X). In particular, if X=[Xb,Xw] with every column of Xb cluster-constant and every column of Xw cluster-centred, then least squares is generalized least squares and every least squares estimate of an estimable function is best linear unbiased.

  3. Let 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β be estimable and let 𝛌c=X(X⊤X)−λ, so that 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β^=c⊤y. If c is cluster-constant then 𝛌𝛃Var(λ⊤β^)={1+(m−1)ρ}⋅σ2‖c‖2, and if c is cluster-centred then 𝛌𝛃Var(λ⊤β^)=(1−ρ)σ2‖c‖2. In both cases σ2‖c‖2 is the variance the estimate would have under 𝛆Cov(ε)=σ2I; the multiplier is the design effect. In either case 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β^ is best linear unbiased even if (b) fails.

  4. Suppose C(X)=Sb⊕Sw with Sb⊆C(PW) of dimension pb and Sw⊆C(PW)⊥ of dimension pw=p−pb. Then the usual residual mean square has E(s2)=λw(G−pb)+λs(n−G−pw)n−p,{#eq-cls-naive-s2}

    and for any c as in (c) the usual variance estimate 𝛌𝛌v=s2λ⊤(X⊤X)−λ satisfies 𝛌𝛃E(v)/Var(λ⊤β^)=E(s2)/λ, with λ=λw or λs according to the stratum of c.

prp-cls-growth.title: The balanced random-coefficient growth model
prp-cls-growth.html:
Assume @eq-cls-random-coefficient with a common X of full column rank p≤m, and D positive definite. Write K=X⊤X, C=σ2K−1, S=D+C, and let bi=K−1X⊤yi be subject i’s own least squares coefficient vector.

  1. C(ΣX)⊆C(X), so ordinary and generalized least squares coincide, and 𝛃𝛃β^=K−1X⊤y¯=b¯,Cov(β^)=D+σ2K−1N=SN,{#eq-cls-growth-beta}

    exactly, for every N. No covariance parameter is needed to estimate the population curve.

  2. The best linear unbiased predictor of ui (@thm-mix-blup, which is @thm-cor-blup applied coordinatewise with x0=0) is 𝛃𝛃u^i=DX⊤Σ−1(yi−Xβ^)=W(bi−β^),W=DS−1,{#eq-cls-growth-blup}

    with W=D(D+C)−1 and Cov(u^i−ui)=D−(1−1/N)WD. The predicted curve of subject i is 𝛃X(β^+u^i), with 𝛃𝛃Cov(β^+u^i−β−ui)=(D−1+C−1)−1+(I−W)CN.{#eq-cls-growth-pev}

  3. The restricted maximum likelihood estimates of σ2 and D are σ^2=1N(m−p)∑i=1N‖yi−Xbi‖2,D^=Sb−σ^2K−1,{#eq-cls-growth-reml}

    where Sb=(N−1)−1∑i(bi−b¯)(bi−b¯)⊤, provided D^ is nonnegative definite.

prp-cls-multivariate.title: The multivariate test
prp-cls-multivariate.html: Under the assumptions of @thm-cls-sphericity with N≥m, let Sz=W/(N−1) and T2=Nz¯⊤Sz−1z¯. Then T2 does not depend on the choice of U, nor on replacing U by UK for any nonsingular (m−1)×(m−1) matrix K; and under H, N−m+1(N−1)(m−1)T2∼F(m−1,N−m+1), whatever Σ is. The distributional statement is Hotelling’s and is not proved here; see Anderson (2003, §5.2).

prp-cls-selection.title: Working covariances, likelihood comparisons and empirical standard errors
prp-cls-selection.title_html:
Working covariances, likelihood comparisons and empirical standard
errors
prp-cls-selection.html:
Let the N subjects be independent, with 𝛃E(Yi)=Xiβ and true covariance Σi0. Let 𝛉Σi(θ) be a working covariance model whose eigenvalues are bounded above and away from zero uniformly in i and, for fixed 𝛉θ, let 𝛃𝛉𝛉𝛉𝛉𝛉β~(θ)=A(θ)−1∑iXi⊤Σi(θ)−1Yi,A(θ)=∑iXi⊤Σi(θ)−1Xi, assumed nonsingular.

  1. 𝛃𝛉β~(θ) is unbiased for every 𝛉θ, whether or not the working model is correct, with exact covariance A−1BA−1 where B=∑iXi⊤Σi−1Σi0Σi−1Xi. If the working model is correct, B=A and the covariance is A−1.

  2. The empirical covariance estimate U^E replaces Σi0 by riri⊤, with 𝛃ri=Yi−Xiβ~. Under the conditions (K1)–(K3) of Section 33.2, applied with 𝛉Σi(θ)−1Xi in place of Xi, it satisfies n(U^E−A−1BA−1)→0 in probability as N→∞, whatever Σi0 is.

  3. Let K be any n×(n−p) matrix whose columns form an orthonormal basis of C(X)⊥. The restricted log likelihood of a covariance model is the log likelihood of K⊤Y (@def-mix-reml) and does not depend on the choice of K (@thm-mix-reml). Hence two covariance models fitted with the same X have restricted likelihoods that are densities of one and the same random vector, and their difference is a genuine log likelihood ratio. If the models differ in X, the two are densities of different random vectors and cannot be compared.

thm-cls-sphericity.title: Sphericity is necessary and sufficient for the exact F test
thm-cls-sphericity.title_html: Sphericity is necessary and sufficient for the exact F test
thm-cls-sphericity.html:
Let y1,…,yN be independent 𝛍Nm(μ,Σ) with Σ positive definite, m≥2, N≥2, and let F be the statistic built from @eq-cls-rm-ss. Put Ψ=U⊤ΣU, q=Nz¯ and W=∑i(zi−z¯)(zi−z¯)⊤.

  1. SST=‖q‖2 and SSE=tr(W), and under H the vector q∼Nm−1(0,Ψ) is independent of W∼Wm−1(N−1,Ψ). Hence F=N(N−1)‖z¯‖2/tr(W).

  2. If Σ satisfies sphericity, then under H F∼F(m−1,(N−1)(m−1)) exactly, for every N≥2.

  3. Conversely, if the null distribution of F is F(m−1,(N−1)(m−1)) for every N≥2, then Σ satisfies sphericity.

thm-cls-splitplot.title: The balanced split-plot design
thm-cls-splitplot.html:
Assume @eq-cls-splitplot-model with r,a,b≥2, and write the cell means μijk=E(yijk). Let M be the orthogonal projection onto the model space C(X)=C(P0+PB+PA+PC+PAC).

  1. C(VX)⊆C(X), so least squares is generalized least squares and every least squares estimate of an estimable function is its best linear unbiased estimator, whatever σw2 and σs2 are.

  2. The sums of squares are those of the balanced three-way layout, with SSA=rb∑j(y¯⋅j⋅−y¯⋅⋅⋅)2, SSC=ra∑k(y¯⋅⋅k−y¯⋅⋅⋅)2, SSAC=r∑j,k(y¯⋅jk−y¯⋅j⋅−y¯⋅⋅k+y¯⋅⋅⋅)2, and the two error sums of squares SSAB=‖PABy‖2 and SSE=‖PEy‖2.

  3. The expected mean squares (@thm-ss-expected-mean-squares) are EMSB=λw+abr−1∑i(ξi−ξ¯)2,EMSAB=λw=σs2+bσw2,EMSA=λw+rba−1∑j(αj−α¯)2,EMSE=λs=σs2,EMSC=λs+rab−1∑k(κk−κ¯)2,EMSAC=λs+r(a−1)(b−1)∑j,kδjk2,{#eq-cls-splitplot-ems}

    where αj=ωj+γ¯j⋅, κk=τk+γ¯⋅k and δjk=γjk−γ¯j⋅−γ¯⋅k+γ¯ are the equal-weight effects of @def-tw-interaction computed from μ¯⋅jk.

  4. Under normality the six sums of squares are independent, SSAB/λw∼χ2((r−1)(a−1)), SSE/λs∼χ2((r−1)a(b−1)), and MSAMSAB∼F(a−1,(r−1)(a−1),rbλw∑j(αj−α¯)2), while MSC/MSE and MSAC/MSE have noncentral F distributions on (b−1,(r−1)a(b−1)) and ((a−1)(b−1),(r−1)a(b−1)) degrees of freedom with noncentralities ra∑k(κk−κ¯)2/λs and r∑j,kδjk2/λs. So the whole-plot factor is tested against MSAB and the subplot factor and the interaction against MSE.

  5. A contrast ∑jcjαj is estimated by ∑jcjy¯⋅j⋅ with variance λw∑jcj2/(rb); a contrast ∑kdkκk is estimated by ∑kdky¯⋅⋅k with variance λs∑kdk2/(ra). Both are best linear unbiased, and the two estimators are uncorrelated.

  6. Fix a subplot treatment k and a contrast ∑jcj=0. The simple effect ∑jcjμ¯⋅jk is estimated by ∑jcjy¯⋅jk, best linear unbiased, with variance (∑jcj2)λw+(b−1)λsrb=(∑jcj2)σw2+σs2r,{#eq-cls-splitplot-simple}

    which belongs to neither stratum: no single mean square estimates it, and the unbiased estimate is the combination (∑jcj2){MSAB+(b−1)MSE}/(rb).
